node-1.label: A 53-year-old male has had multiple dusky reddish nodules on the trunk for 7 years

node-2.label: The nodules are bilaterally distributed along the lateral sides of the trunk and have shown slight progression

node-3.label: The patient has a medical history of arterial hypertension and type 2 diabetes mellitus

node-4.label: There were no systemic symptoms indicating involvement of other organs, and no specific triggers causing induction or exacerbation were reported

node-5.label: Stroking the lesions resulted in swelling, itching, and redness of the skin

attrs.why: New biopsy shows CD117/toluidine-blue-positive dermal mast cells, confirming a mast cell disorder and strongly supporting cutaneous mastocytosis. The chronic bilateral truncal nodules with a Darier sign and absence of systemic symptoms favor skin-limited urticaria pigmentosa, consistent with expert pathologist and laboratory opinion. The additional mixed B-cell infiltrate does not negate this diagnosis.

Darier sign and skin mast cells support a mast cell disorder, but no systemic symptoms, no organomegaly data showing involvement, and PET/CT without hypermetabolic lesions argue against extracutaneous disease. However, tryptase and KIT D816V results are not yet available, so systemic mastocytosis is not fully excluded; confidence remains low.

Darier sign with itching, swelling, and redness could suggest an urticarial reaction, but the chronic truncal nodules and biopsy findings of CD117/toluidine-blue-positive mast cells favor cutaneous mastocytosis rather than isolated chronic urticarial dermatosis. No specific triggers are reported, so the likelihood of chronic urticarial dermatosis is reduced.
node-3 hypertension and type 2 diabetes are comorbidities; node-5 Darier sign and node-4 no triggers refute metabolic cause.

node-10.label: Skin biopsy shows dermal mast cells positive for CD117 and toluidine blue

node-11.label: Skin biopsy shows infiltration by atypical lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells

node-12.label: Ig heavy chain rearrangement demonstrates B-cell monoclonality

node-13.label: Serum IgG is elevated at 1905.80 mg/dL

node-14.label: PET/CT shows no hypermetabolic metastatic lesions

node-15.label: Concurrent cutaneous B-cell lymphoproliferative disorder with mast cell disorder

attrs.why: Pathologist reports atypical lymphocytes, eosinophils, and plasma cells on biopsy, Ig heavy chain rearrangement showing B-cell monoclonality, elevated serum IgG, and PET/CT without hypermetabolic metastasis, suggesting a possible concurrent cutaneous B-cell lymphoproliferative process. The finding is not definitive and may be reactive, so confidence is moderate.
